lower reoffending when family ties are maintained

settings.title: make engineers — schools & youth
settings.body: Curriculum-mapped, OCN-accredited engineering programmes for ages 11–19: from a working bamboo speaker to a rideable bamboo bike. Real making that reaches young people — including those the system is failing — before the justice system does.

settings.title: build to bond — prisons
settings.body: A six-week bamboo bike-building course inside prison workshops. Makers earn an OCN Level 2 in Sustainable Design & Manufacturing and finish by giving the bike they built to their own child on family visit day.

settings.title: input
settings.body: A workshop, bamboo, tools and a trained instructor — in a school, a community space or a prison industries workshop. Funded by kit and workshop sales, grants and partners.

settings.title: activity
settings.body: Hands-on building: measuring, mitring, bonding and finishing a real bamboo frame. No prior experience — the craft is the teacher.

settings.title: output
settings.body: A finished bike, a portfolio of work, and a nationally recognised OCN qualification — Level 1 Award (Practical Manufacturing Skills) in schools, Level 2 (Sustainable Design & Manufacturing) in prisons.

settings.title: outcome
settings.body: Skills that map to real trades, confidence built by making something that works — and, inside prison, a family bond strengthened when the bike goes home with a Maker's child.

settings.title: impact
settings.body: Better routes into work, education and training — and a contribution to the two levers the evidence says matter most on release: employment and family ties. We contribute to these outcomes; we don't claim them alone.
